To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) BDM is the best classification technique for the classification of human daily activities; and (ii) the combination of LSM and k-NN is the best classification method for the classification of sports activities.
BDM is the best classifier for the classification of human activities using bodyworn inertial/magnetic sensor units.

(a) the best classification results are achieved using BDM with SFFS, (b) the classification results are improved when using the magnetometer, (c) the best classification rates are obtained when using the accelerometer, (d) the classification results improve with the increase of the number of features, and (e) the best classification performance is obtained when using all the sensor units.

developing a system to automatically identify the human activities performed using bodywornsensors.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BDM is the best choice for real-time applications, and SVM is the best choice if computational complexity is not a concern.
the best performing classifier for human activity recognition depends on several factors such as the number of sensors, number of features, and type of activities.
there is no single classifier that is superior to all the others, and the best classifier to be used depends on the application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BDM method is the most suitable method for human activity classification using bodyworn inertial/magnetic sensors.
the BDM classifier with PCA feature reduction is the best choice for classifying human activities using miniature inertial and/or magnetic sensors.
BDM with PCA and SFFS is a good candidate for classifying daily and sports activities in a real-time environment using body-worn miniature inertial/magnetic sensor units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of BDM with SFFS can be used as a simple, yet effective, approach for classifying human activities.
the choice of a classifier should be based on the application and the number of features used.

the classification of human activities using body-worn sensors is a challenging task and the performance of the classifiers depends on the features used, the number of sensors, the sensor placement, and the number of subjects.
